call_points.text: Aims to install at least 1 crore smart meters in FY27 against annual capacity of over 1.8 crore meters.
Order book including SPVs and the GIC Platform was about ₹24,020 Cr as on 30 June 2026, excluding taxes.
About 8–9 crore electricity meters are expected to be tendered in FY27, out of 31–32 crore meters to go smart.
Expects 50-75 days improvement in working-capital days in FY27, with positive operating cash flow from FY28.
O&M revenue expected to reach ₹600–700 Cr from FY28, rising to ₹1,100–1,200 Cr as the installed base matures.
Gas metering opportunity in India estimated at ₹35,000–36,000 Cr over the next 3–4 years.
Sees about ₹500 Cr of international business potential over the next 3–4 years.
All projects have achieved operational go-live, which management expects to progressively ease working-capital intensity.
Contracts are fixed price with no pass-through, so the company absorbs commodity and currency moves.
Net debt rose to ₹1,573 Cr at March 2026 from ₹605 Cr a year earlier, mostly short-term loans.
Peak net debt seen at about ₹1,900-2,000 Cr, with short-term loans starting to reduce from FY28.
All 24 AMISP projects covering 3.61 crore meters have achieved operational go-live.
Plans another ₹600-700 Cr investment in the GIC joint venture platform over FY27, FY28 and Q1FY29.
O&M revenue was about ₹150 Cr in FY26 and is expected to reach ₹800 Cr a year within two to three years.
Targets ₹500 Cr of export revenue over the next two to three years, with meaningful numbers from this financial year.
Declined to give FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance, asking for one more quarter.

O&M revenue was about ₹150 Cr in FY26 and is expected to reach ₹800 Cr a year within two to three years on the current order book.
Total order book including all SPVs and the GIC Platform was about ₹24,020 Cr (excluding taxes) as on 30 June 2026.
Annual production capacity is over 1.8 crore meters; the company aims to install at least 1 crore smart meters in FY27.
